title: Flaky Test Detective
description: A flaky test passes and fails on the same code. The detective runs your test suite several times and flags the tests whose result changes from one run to the next.
noData: No analysis yet. Run your tests several times, or analyse the test reports already in the project.
summaryRun: {{flaky}} flaky out of {{total}} tests, over {{runs}} runs of {{command}}
summaryScan: {{flaky}} flaky out of {{total}} tests, from {{reports}} test reports

fixes.timing: Replace fixed sleeps and timeouts with explicit waits or polling, or raise the timeout.
fixes.test_order: Make each test set up and clean up its own state so it no longer depends on the order tests run in.
fixes.shared_state: Isolate shared state per test: a fresh database transaction or an in-memory store per test.
fixes.network: Mock external network calls (WireMock, nock, responses…) instead of reaching real services.
fixes.randomness: Seed random generators and use fixed GUIDs, UUIDs and dates in tests.
fixes.resource_leak: Close files, connections and handles in the teardown (Dispose, afterEach, tearDown).
fixes.concurrency: Synchronise shared access and use thread-safe assertions.
fixes.environment: Pin environment variables and system dependencies, for example by running tests in a container.
fixes.unknown: Run the test on its own several times to confirm it, and add logging around the failing assertion.

run.noCommand: No supported test command was found in this project. Supported: .NET (dotnet test), pytest, Vitest, Jest with jest-junit, Maven, Gradle and Go.
run.help: Each run executes the whole suite and writes its report to .workpilot/flaky-tests/, so later analyses take it into account too. .NET builds once, then reuses that build.

errors.noProject: Select a project before running a scan.
errors.no_command: No supported test command was found in this project.
errors.no_results: The test command wrote no test report: it probably failed before running the tests (build error, missing tool). Its output:
errors.no_tests: The test command ran without running a single test: what it targets probably holds no test. Its output:
errors.no_dotnet_tests: This .NET project has no test project (xUnit, NUnit, MSTest or TUnit): dotnet test would build and run nothing. Add a test project (for example dotnet new xunit) and run again.

verdict.likely_bug: Fails in more than 80% of the runs: more likely a real bug than a flaky test.
verdict.flaky: Fails in 20% of the runs or more: confirmed flaky.
verdict.rare: Fails rarely (under 20% of the runs): run it again to confirm.

history.ciOnly: Fails only in CI, never in a local run: look at what CI changes (fewer CPUs, containers, parallel jobs, clock).

suspects.hint: Too long to run the whole suite again? Run only these tests.
suspects.ranOnly: This run kept {{count}} suspect test(s) only.

quarantine.pytest: Mark the test `@pytest.mark.xfail(reason="flaky: <link to this card>", strict=False)` so it still runs but no longer fails the suite, and register a `quarantine` marker if the project lists its markers.
quarantine.vitest: Move the test into a `*.quarantine.test.ts` file excluded from the default `vitest run` (the `exclude` of the config) and run by a separate, non-blocking CI step.
quarantine.jest: Move the test into a `*.quarantine.test.js` file left out by `testPathIgnorePatterns` and run by a separate, non-blocking CI step.
quarantine.js: Move the test to a file the default test command leaves out, run by a separate, non-blocking CI step.
quarantine.dotnet: Add the framework's category (`[Trait("Category", "Quarantine")]` for xUnit, `[Category("Quarantine")]` for NUnit, `[TestCategory("Quarantine")]` for MSTest), filter it out of the blocking CI step (`--filter Category!=Quarantine`) and run it in a separate, non-blocking step.
quarantine.jvm: Tag the test `@Tag("quarantine")` (JUnit 5), exclude the tag from the blocking build (Surefire `excludedGroups`, Gradle `excludeTags`) and run it in a separate, non-blocking job.
quarantine.go: Skip the test unless `QUARANTINE=1` (`if os.Getenv("QUARANTINE") == "" { t.Skip("flaky: <link>") }`) and run `QUARANTINE=1 go test -run` in a separate, non-blocking CI step.
quarantine.rust: Mark the test `#[ignore = "flaky: <link>"]` and run `cargo test -- --ignored` in a separate, non-blocking CI step.
quarantine.ruby: Tag the example `:quarantine`, exclude the tag from the blocking run (`--tag ~quarantine`) and run it in a separate, non-blocking step.
quarantine.php: Add the test to a `quarantine` group (`#[Group('quarantine')]`), exclude it from the blocking run (`--exclude-group quarantine`) and run it in a separate, non-blocking step.
quarantine.swift: Move the test into a separate test plan or scheme that CI runs without blocking.
quarantine.dart: Tag the test `quarantine`, exclude the tag from the blocking run (`--exclude-tags quarantine`) and run it in a separate, non-blocking step.
quarantine.elixir: Tag the test `@tag :quarantine`, exclude it in `test_helper.exs` and run `mix test --only quarantine` in a separate, non-blocking step.
quarantine.other: Use the test framework's own way to keep the test running in a separate, non-blocking suite, out of the blocking one.

fix.title: Fix the flaky test {{name}}
fix.intro: This test passes and fails on the same code. Find why and make it deterministic.
fix.rules:
Fix the cause, not the symptom: no skip, no retry, and a longer timeout alone is not a fix.
The test must still fail when the behaviour it checks breaks.
If the test shows a real bug (it fails almost every time), fix the code, not the test.
fix.criteria:
{{name}} passes in 10 runs in a row.
{{name}} still fails when the behaviour it checks is broken.
The rest of the suite stays green.

quarantine.title: Quarantine the flaky test {{name}}
quarantine.intro: This test passes and fails on the same code. Until it is fixed, keep it running without blocking CI.
quarantine.rules:
The test keeps running, in a separate suite that does not block CI: it is not deleted or emptied.
The quarantine names this card, so it can be lifted once the test is fixed.
Nothing else changes in the blocking suite.
quarantine.criteria:
{{name}} no longer blocks CI.
{{name}} still runs, in the quarantine suite.
The rest of the suite stays green.
